question: What is the function of the yellow change interval, how is its duration established, and may a pre-yellow vehicular countdown display be used?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The yellow change interval's sole function is to warn approaching traffic that its permission to proceed is ending, after which vehicles will be directed to stop (or, for protected/permissive turns, must complete the turn permissively). Its duration must be determined using engineering practices, with a recommended range of 3 to 6 seconds (longer values reserved for higher-speed approaches). Pre-yellow vehicular countdown displays may NOT be used: the MUTCD expressly prohibits signal displays intended to provide a "pre-yellow warning" at signalized locations, because research has found they increase crash frequency. Standards (mandatory): - "The duration of the yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices." - For pedestrian hybrid beacons: "The duration of the steady yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices in accordance with the provisions in Section 4F.17." - For emergency-vehicle hybrid beacons: "The duration of the steady yellow change interval shall be determined using engineering practices in accordance with the provisions in Section 4F.17." - As shown on the Section 4F.17 page [Image 2]: "Except for Warning Beacons mounted on advance warning signs on the approach to a signalized location (see Section 2C.35), signal displays that are intended to provide a 'pre-yellow warning' interval, such as flashing green signal indications, vehicular countdown displays, or other similar displays, shall not be used at a signalized location." Guidance (recommended): - "A yellow change interval should have a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 6 seconds (see Section 4F.17). The longer intervals should be reserved for use on approaches with higher speeds." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 4I-4 shows the yellow change interval (of at least 3 seconds) in its possible relationships with the pedestrian buffer interval and red clearance interval. - [Image 2] shows Section 4F.17 in full, including the Support statement of the interval's exclusive warning function, the Standard requiring engineering practices for its duration, the 3–6 second Guidance, and the Standard prohibiting pre-yellow warning displays such as vehicular countdown displays. - [Image 3] shows Figure 4I-4 in context in Section 4I.06, illustrating how the yellow change interval relates to pedestrian intervals. - [Image 4] shows related Standards that the yellow change interval shall not be shortened or omitted during preemption and priority control transitions. - [Image 5] shows Section 4H.11 applying the Section 4F.17 duration provisions to bicycle signal phases and explaining the interval's warning function for bicyclists. Citations: - Section 4F.17 Support §1 (p.708) - Section 4F.17 Standard §3 (p.708) - Section 4H.11 Support §3 (p.717) - Section 4N.03 Standard §4 (p.743) - Section 4J.03 Standard §10 (p.730) - Section 4N.03 Guidance §5 (p.743) - Figure 4I-4 (p.724) - Page 749
gold_answer: The yellow change interval warns that permission to proceed or a protected movement is ending. Its duration must be determined using engineering practices, with guidance of 3 to 6 seconds. Pre-yellow displays such as vehicular countdowns or flashing green indications are prohibited, except for permitted advance-warning beacons.
